summary: The video is a comprehensive, technique-heavy walkthrough of landscape processing in Lightroom/Camera Raw and Photoshop, focused on the “zone” approach to editing desert and canyon imagery. The host demonstrates starting with a deliberately flat, high-dynamic-range look, then non-destructively developing light and color through a sequence of steps that emphasize whites for glow, selective color, and color grading. He illustrates moving from one-zone shots to more complex multi-zone composites, including sky replacement, cloud manipulation, and the layering of light and depth. The narrative covers practical editing workflows (history states, clone stamp, puppet and perspective warp, de-haze), strategies for guiding the viewer’s eye, and the philosophical stance that many “abstract” desert images require only modest processing compared with grand landscapes. Several concrete examples (including a Castleton sunrise reference) anchor the discussion, and the presenter repeatedly emphasizes time-efficient, zone-aware editing as a core skill for landscape images.

sections.title: Intro and zone philosophy in Painted Deserts
sections.description: The host opens by referencing other Painted Deserts videos and emphasizes the zone-based processing approach, noting the area’s strong compositions and absence of dead spaces.

sections.title: Initial RAW prep: dynamic range expansion and flat starting point
sections.description: The video describes expanding the dynamic range to create a flat, boring starting point, then suppressing exposure to leave room for developing light and color later in the workflow.

sections.title: Non-destructive history workflow into Photoshop
sections.description: The presenter records the editing steps in Photoshop history so adjustments can be revisited nondestructively, with a commitment to using Photoshop for its history capabilities.

sections.title: One-zone processing and minimal Photoshop usage
sections.description: The speaker prioritizes one-zone processing for easier edits, highlighting the Whites technique and minimal Photoshop steps for flat images rather than multi-layer manipulations.

sections.title: Depth, depth cues, and light painting in multi-zone work
sections.description: The discussion shifts to introducing depth through selective blurring, layered adjustments, and painting light along ridges. The host demonstrates how to separate foreground/background zones and use brushes and light to guide the viewer’s eye through the frame.

sections.title: Sky manipulation, cloud layers, and final multi-zone composites
sections.description: In the concluding portion, the host showcases five-zone (and multi-zone) composites, cloud layer placement, sky substitutions, tonal adjustments, and final refinements, culminating in a vivid, depth-filled landscape with intentional light directions.

featured_techniques.technique: Dynamic range expansion to create a flat starting image
Whites replacement to create glow and drive color
Non-destructive editing using History and Photoshop recording
Background blur to imply depth via painting with a level of blacks transition
Directional side-light painting with hard/soft edge brushes
Sky replacement using clone stamp and blending modes
Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp for selective warping
Auto HDR for cloud texture and texture enhancement
Tonal-based color adjustments to fix sky inconsistencies
Rule of trapezoids for extended wide-angle feel
Dehaze and color balance to sculpt stormy skies
Cloud cloning with color-bound blending to fake clouds
